function: Channel prediction: predicts J future channel frames of an XL-MIMO UE from P past estimated frames, reducing pilot overhead (p. 3-4)
system: XL-MIMO BS with 128x128 UPA (8x8 subarrays), single-antenna UE moving at 20 m/s, 30 GHz near-field, spatially non-stationary; no RIS (p. 1, 4)
method: CNN-Transformer encoder-decoder (CTCP), supervised with NMSE loss on LS/MMSE-estimated channels; two-stage training then prediction, learning rate 1e-4, 50 epochs (p. 3-4)
data_channel: Own simulator: last-bounce-cluster near-field XL-MIMO model with birth-death scatterers, 30 GHz; 16000/2000/2000 training/validation/testing samples (p. 2, 4)
test_conditions: Same simulated channel model for training and testing (2000 test samples); prediction length J up to 40 and Rician factor kappa swept (p. 4-5)
baselines: Learned only: GRU, LSTM, Transformer [11], L-TF, G-TF, CL-TF, ConvL-TF [10]; no non-learned predictor such as Kalman or autoregression is compared (p. 5)
metrics: NMSE training loss; NMSE(dB) per FLOP (eta) and achievable rate per FLOP (rho) versus prediction length and Rician factor; FLOPs (p. 4-5)
complexity: FLOPs in Table II: CTCP 14.3x10^6 for 128x128 antennas and 57.2x10^6 for 256x256, compared with LSTM, GRU, Transformer and hybrid models (p. 4)
q1_support: p. 1: "we first construct a last-bounce cluster (LBC)-based channel to capture the near-field propagation"; a custom simulator (birth-death scatterers, p. 2), not 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "η against different κ is shown in Fig. 6(d)"; the paper sweeps prediction length and Rician factor on its own simulator and never states that a model trained under one condition is tested under another (Table I, p. 4: 16000, 2000 and 2000 training, validation and test samples).
q3_support: p. 5: "compared to other DL-based channel prediction methods, such as GRU [13], LSTM [13], Transformer (TF) [11]"; all baselines are learned, and no Kalman, autoregressive or outdated-channel predictor is compared in Figs. 5-6 or Table II.
q4_support: p. 4: "TABLE II shows the neural network floating point operations (FLOPs)"; Table II lists 14.3 x 10^6 FLOPs for CTCP at 128 x 128 antennas and 57.2 x 10^6 at 256 x 256, against seven learned baselines.
q5_support: p. 4: "The simulation parameters are provided in TABLE I."; the data come from the authors' own LBC simulator, and the letter gives no code or data link, DOI, or public or measured dataset.
notes: Prediction of future channel frames from past estimated ones is area 2. The channel is the authors' LBC simulator (birth-death scatterers after [5], [12]), not 3GPP, so q1 is 0. No non-learned predictor (Kalman, autoregressive) is compared in the results, so q3 is 0. Table I and Table II values were read from the page image.
